span.label: method
span.quote: To this end, we develop a method that can be used to learn policies that map raw image observations directly to torques at the robot’s motors.

span.label: visuomotor policy learning
span.quote: In this section, we define the visuomotor policy learning problem and present an overview of our approach.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We address these challenges by developing a guided policy search algorithm for sensorimotor deep learning, as well as a novel CNN architecture designed for robotic control.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: guided policy search: convert reinforcement-learning policy search into supervised learning of a deep network, with a trajectory-optimizer acting as the teacher
span.quote: guided policy search method, which transforms policy search into supervised learning

span.label: training requires positioning objects at consistent positions
span.note: what this limits: the training procedure as described: it requires TO POSITION THE OBJECTS IN THE SCENE AT CONSISTENT POSITIONS
span.quote: to position the objects in the scene at consistent positions

span.label: The method does not generalise to dramatically different visual settings, especially under occluding distractors.
span.note: what this limits: the generalisation claim: OUR CURRENT METHOD DOES NOT GENERALIZE TO DRAMATICALLY DIFFERENT SETTINGS, ESPECIALLY WHEN VISUAL DISTRACTO[rs occlude]
span.quote: Although we demonstrate moderate generalization over variations in the scene, our current method does not generalize to dramatically different settings, especially when visual distractors occlude the manipulated object or break up its silhouette in ways that differ from the training.

span.label: The approach requires the full system state to be observable during training, which restricts the range of applicable tasks.
span.note: what this limits: the range of tasks the method can address: THE REQUIREMENT TO OBSERVE THE FULL STATE DURING TRAINING LIMITS THE TASKS TO WHICH THE METHOD CAN BE APPLIED
span.quote: However, the requirement to observe the full state during training limits the tasks to which the method can be applied.

span.label: Tasks with freely moving objects would need heavier instrumentation such as motion capture.
span.note: what this limits: any extension to freely moving objects: those TASKS ... REQUIRE MORE EXTENSIVE INSTRUMENTATION, SUCH AS MOTION CAPTURE
span.quote: However, tasks that require, for example, manipulating freely moving objects require more extensive instrumentation, such as motion capture.

span.label: The spatial feature-point representation makes simplifying assumptions about feature presence and uniqueness.
span.note: what this limits: every result produced through the visual encoder: THE FEATURE POINT REPRESENTATION ... ASSUMES THAT THE LEARNED FEATURES ARE PRESENT AT ALL TIMES, AND ONLY ONE INSTANCE OF EACH FEATURE IS EVER PRESENT IN THE IMAGE
span.quote: The feature point representation is very simple, since it assumes that the learned features are present at all times, and only one instance of each feature is ever present in the image.

span.label: The method needs the full state observable during training, and the authors say exactly when that is minor and when it is not.
span.note: what this limits: applying this method to a new task: the full state must be observable during training, which the authors call minor when objects can be positioned consistently and not minor for tasks manipulating freely moving objects
span.quote: However, the requirement to observe the full state during training limits the tasks to which the method can be applied. In many cases, this limitation is minor, and the only “instrumentation” required at training is to position the objects in the scene at consistent positions. span.note: what this limits: the architecture comparison in this paper: it is measured on the pose-estimation pretraining task, described by the authors as a reasonable proxy for the visuomotor challenges
span.quote: To isolate the architectures from other confounding factors, we measure their accuracy on the pose estimation pretraining task described in Section 5.2. This is a reasonable proxy for evaluating how well the network can overcome two major challenges in visuomotor learning

span.label: The training-time observability the method depends on is bought with a physical constraint on the world, stated plainly: providing the full state 'simply requires positioning objects in one of several known positions for each trial during training'. The assumption is not about the algorithm but about how the laboratory is arranged.
